- Windows 95 taskbar (measured against a real-Windows study): the pressed task button has the 2x2 chequer pattern, the open Start button carries the dotted focus box, and the clock well is a single sunken line.
- Windows 11 taskbar buttons use WinUI's 4 dp control corner radius.
- Windows 11 colours checked against WinUI's own resource files (text 1A1A1A on light, secondary text C9C9C9 on dark); corners 4 dp controls / 8 dp panels already match.
- Windows 11 Settings pages are see-through when opened full screen too (not only as a window).
- Windows 11 launcher settings: the "Open the launcher to test" button (starts the launcher without making it the default home app) is back at the top.
- Windows 11: the Start menu is narrower on a turned phone and tablet; windows open at 60% of the turned screen's width; dark Windows 11 toggles and accents use the Windows blue instead of white; long category folder names (Communication) show whole.
- Windows 11 search: the panel rises above the keyboard; settings results open Pulse's own Settings page in a window (not the phone's page); typing you / tube / ytx lists YTXTube.
- Windows 11 quick settings: nine tiles to a page (3x3) with pages one under the other and dots, new tiles (Screenshot, Private DNS, Dark mode, NFC, Sync; Screenshot, DNS and dark mode need root or Shizuku), and a pencil to choose which tiles show.
- Add gadgets: the music, Winamp, video, lyrics and noise widgets show the live widget as their preview instead of a plain white note.
- Windows 11 and 10: the Start button held opens the Win+X menu (Apps and Features, Power Options, System, Task Manager, Settings, Control Panel, Terminal, Registry Editor, File Explorer, Search, Run), acrylic in 11 and flat in 10. Quick tiles held open their own settings page.
- Windows 11 Settings: Back from a launcher settings page (Taskbar, Start ...) returns to the Personalization list, not the first Settings page.
- Phone wallpaper follows the launcher while Pulse is the home app (the phone's own wallpaper is saved first and returns when another launcher is the home app, the switch is turned off, or with the button in Look).
- Keyboard: a picture in the bar's right slot shows no file name (its preview is enough).
- Wallpaper picker: phone pictures stand upright (their own rows), desktop pictures lie; the list scrolls and starts the HD download of the look's pack by itself. The phone wallpaper set from the launcher uses the HD file when it is installed.
- Apps: a picture of your own for any app or file (menu: Change icon / Reset icon), shown everywhere the launcher draws it; menu has Pin to desktop; App info is Pulse's own Properties page; apps held in the Windows 11 search results open the same menu.
- Personalize in the desktop's menu opens in a window on the Windows looks (Windows 11: the Personalization page) instead of a full black screen.
- Material, One UI and ColorOS launcher looks: the phone's own wallpaper shows behind the launcher (a light veil), a custom wallpaper from Look is drawn too; AMOLED stays pure black.
- Launcher settings > Home screen: Set up like my phone (the owner's folders System, TC, Technic and Ai, the tools hidden from the apps list, the dock Phone, Messages and Camera, and a 5 x 6 grid); runs only when asked. Apps hidden from the list still show inside folders.
- Files: the Secure Folder move icon's arrow shows on every look; the Secure Folder's user number is read from the phone instead of assuming 150. Set up like my phone also places Pulse's weather and music widgets.
- Keyboard: more than five pictures arriving together that are not camera photos or screenshots (a zip opened, a folder copied) no longer take the bar's right slot.
- Code: Open with Code (a new entry in the phone's Open with list, any file type) opens the file as text; Code has icons on Open and New and a menu of three lines with Open, New and the projects.
- Files: .md and plain text files of any name open in Files' own text viewer again (the code editor stays in the file's menu and Open as); code files still open in the code editor.
- Keyboard: the floating keyboard is a little wider by default (88 percent of the full size) unless its size was set by hand.
- Files: a .lrc lyrics file opens in a lyrics editor: the song of the same name beside it plays, a tap on a time goes there, Stamp gives the chosen line the time of the song now, +-0.1 s nudges it, lines can be added and edited, and it saves back to the file.
- Keyboard: the floating keyboard has its own number row switch, off by default (the digits come by holding a letter).
- Files: the archive icon of a file that is no archive compresses at once (no menu of one entry); an archive still shows its menu (open, extract, add, info).
- Files as the file picker: the kinds an app asks for (several at once, like pptx and ppt) are read, other files are dim and cannot be chosen, also in Recent; the Recent list reads the phone's newest files in pages as you scroll (no limit, no wait).
- Launcher: the home grid goes up to 12 x 12; the Material looks can use the phone's own colours (Look > Use the device's colours, Android 12+, off by default).
- Keyboard: a new screenshot, picture, video or downloaded file shows in the bar sooner (first look after a quarter of a second, then three more).
- Launcher extras from the big launchers: a page for each widget (swipe between them, round and round with infinite scroll), two-line names, another grid for the turned phone, hide apps not opened for N days, a daily backup of the settings with restore, a choice of web search engine (Google, DuckDuckGo, Bing, Brave, Yandex, Startpage), a glass dock with its own solidity in the Material looks.
- Launcher: icon animation when tapped (zoom, flip, rotate, bounce); the Material apps list has a category bar (All, Games, Media ...).
- Launcher: infinite scroll for the home icon pages; Wallpaper slides with the pages (the phone's wallpaper, Material looks); a tap on the page dots opens the page overview (every page small; tap to go, arrows to move a page).
- Launcher gestures: two fingers up, down, left and right (each an action of your choice).
- Launcher search (Windows 11 panel, Material apps list): calendar events whose title matches (with the calendar permission).
- Launcher: a news page (RSS and Atom sources of your own, newest first, a tap opens the article), reached from the settings or as a gesture action.
- Material looks: Accent colours picks White, the phone's own colour (Material You) or a colour of the look saved in Palette; the glass dock has a soft sheen.
- Launcher: Smart folders (Look > Home screen): the apps list gathers apps that are in no folder of yours into Games, Media, Communication, Productivity, Maps and System folders by itself, from three apps up; new apps join on their own; works in every look's apps list.
- Launcher: a folder can go in the dock (the folder's menu: Add to dock); a tap on it opens the folder.
- The old Windows looks (95, XP, 7) are left as they were: smart folders, tap animations and going-round pages do not touch them. Windows 10 and 11 have a Messages icon in the tray (bottom right) that opens Pulse's Messages in a window.
- Music: scrolling the lyrics up to their first line stops there; only a new pull that starts at the top closes them.
- Windows 10 and 11: the Win+X menu can be edited (items and order); Windows keyboard shortcuts work from a physical keyboard or Pulse's keyboard: Win+X, Win+R, Win+E, Win+I, Win+S, Win+D and the Windows key alone for Start; the search finds Control Panel, Registry Editor, Terminal, Task Manager and the other tools by name; the Control Panel is dark and see-through in Windows 11 and shows two columns when there is room. The Messages tray icon is gone again.
